label: copy-phase steps re-reading w/r/a/t (weak, diffuse)
explanation: Fires almost only after the original phase: 16% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step and 83% on copy steps, with nearly nothing during the original input. Copy-phase firing is enriched when the fed-back input is w, r, a or t (about 4-6x lift, 61% of mass), when the output is k or o, when the next output is 1/f/q/h, and at early recall positions (recall_idx 0-4). But every one of these is diffuse: the in_tok predicate has precision of only about 0.1 (dev F1 0.16), and conjunctions with output and next-output sets raise precision to 0.2-0.3 while recall falls below 0.25 (best dev F1 0.23). Strong activations come from specific input/output pairs such as r->o, r->k and w->o in early copy steps, but no simple token or position rule separates active from inactive steps. Activation looks to depend on hidden-state context in a way that is not captured here.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=w (+3.60), phase=2 & in_tok=r (+3.41), phase=2 & in_tok=a (+2.98), phase=2 & in_tok=t (+2.92), orig4=f (+2.09), orig4=1 (+1.99). Lower it: in_tok=1 (-4.46), in_tok=f (-4.46), in_tok=q (-4.20), in_tok=h (-3.61).
